answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a wide wood top band with highlight streaks. It ends in a darker front-edge line at row 6 (L=151), then eave shadow at row 7 (L=103) and a dark outline at row 8. This matches the 'cabinet: top 5 + edge + eave' reference. Below it, rows 9-30 (22 rows) show the front face: shelf compartments with bottles, shelf boards at rows 15, 22 and 29, and vertical side posts. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden shelf with rows of small bottles and books in several colours, a light top plank, and a dark brown frame. Measured facts: 16 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. These put it level with the stall (17) and the well (20) and above the hedge (9). The outline is a tinted dark brown, not near-black. The weakness is the wood. The frame and shelf boards use about 3-4 steps with little grain, and the top plank is a fairly smooth light band with only a few highlight dots. The bottles are small coloured dots on a flat dark back panel, so the shelf is less richly shaded than the stall or the well, which have per-material ramps of 5-6 tones. It is clean and readable and has no sticker outline or large flat fills, but a careful artist would see it as slightly thinner than the stall reference in wood grain and ramp depth.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden shelf with a light top board, a dark brown interior and rows of small coloured bottles. Its outline and frame edges are a dark brown that leans toward the wood, and the measured 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels confirms the tint, so this is not a black sticker line. It has 16 visible tones per 16x16 tile, close to the stall (17) and well (20) and above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The bottle rows and the grain and highlights on the top board give real texture. Where it falls short of the references is the wood ramp, which has about 4 steps against about 6, and 23 total distinct colours against 38-40 for the stall and well. That puts it slightly below the best references, but a careful artist would still accept it beside them.

The frame is shaded in several browns (highlight on the top plank, mid frame, dark inner shadow). The outline is a dark brown that leans toward the wood, not neutral. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, matching the hedge reference and unlike the neutral lamp outline. Visible tones per 16x16 tile are 16, close to the stall (17) and well (20) and well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no large flat fills appear.
